name: Mahoroba Center Children's Square "Himikko Park" まほろばセンター 子ども広場 「ひみっこぱーく」in Sakurai City
description:
We had fun!
This place claims to be the largest indoor playground in western Japan!
The "Mahoroba Center" in front of Sakurai Station and has been renovated into a facility that gathers information on living, such as parenting and health. On the second floor, an indoor playground produced by Bornelund opened in May 2019.
There is a "baby area" where babies can play safely, a "quiet area" for pretend play and assembly play, and an "active area" where you can move your kids can jump around, climbing through tunnels, going down slides,  rotating playground equipment.
It's easy to access in front of the station, and it's indoors, so you don't have to worry about the weather. There are plenty of rest areas, benches, and a space for picture books. Enjoy a fun day with your family!
We personally enjoyed the giant ball pit!

name: Natural Yamato Onsen Nara Kenko Land Nara Plaza Hotel 天然大和温泉　奈良健康ランド　奈良プラザホテル in Tenri City
description:
Get ready to get wet!
It’s indoor theme park where parents and children can happily play. There is an indoor pool and onsen (hot springs), in which family of all ages can indulge.
Nara Kenko Land has 10 types of baths, including a natural hot spring "outdoor bath" and a "nano/high-concentration artificial carbonated bath", a sauna and bedrock bath, an indoor leisure pool (limited times only), an indoor theme park, various restaurants, and even books to read.
It is a hot spring theme park♨ with a corner, a large and a small banquet halls, a kids room, and a childcare center (for ages 0 to 9).
It is very popular spot for Nara residents for the whole family.
The indoor leisure pool is great for when it’s rainy outside, though it’s only opened for limited times.
There is also a water slide with a total length of about 70 meters and a large pool.
There are a few fun attraction for kids at the “Children's Aguagu Square” where you can find the "Bikkuri Water Bucket" where a large amount of water pours down from a height of about 5 meters, and the mini slide "Double Slider" that small children can enjoy.
Leisure pool
Parents and children can both have fun! Nara Wanpaku Land Hashakids is also a very popular indoor theme park with giant air playground equipment.
In this facility, there are various playground equipment that parents and children can enjoy, such as a giant slider with a total length of about 10m, a ball factory, and an educational monitor work by teamLab. (Renewed on March 18, 2023)
After enjoying swimming to your hearts content, you rest in the rest room (napping room).
You can even stay at the attached Nara Plaza Hotel and take a trip to the hot springs as well.
Hot spring (onsen)
Things to note:
・Diapers are allowed to be worn
・It’s open 24 hours, but additional charges apply after hours
・There are snacks and drinks available for purchase
・Floating rings, beach balls, goggles, etc. are available for rental

name: Ikoma Sanjo Amusement Park 生駒山上遊園地 in Ikoma City
description:
Ikoma Sanjo Amusement Park
It’s on top of a Mount Ikoma so you can see great landscape views. At an altitude of 642 meters, it overlooks the Nara Basin and Osaka Plain.
The aerial cycling "Cycle Monorail" that makes full use of the great views can be ridden from age 3 years, and there are many other attractions that kids can enjoy. "Character shows" and "hero shows" are also held on holidays, making it a recommended spot for families with small children.
If you get tired or hungry, there’s even an on-site restarting you can eat at where you can see the beautiful scenery of the Osaka plain while eating.
Things to note:
• It’s high up on a mountain so it can get a bit windy
• Each attraction has age and height restrictions. Please check carefully when using. In addition, attractions may be suspended or operating hours may be changed due to weather or other reasons.

name: NARA GOLDFISH MUSEUM 奈良金魚ミュージアム in Nara City
description:
Shiny
The first permanent goldfish museum was established in Nara Prefecture, one of the three major goldfish production centers in Japan.
The museum has doubled in size and number of goldfish, and reopened on April 27, 2021, with an increased power to become one of the largest goldfish entertainment aquariums in Japan. It displays 3,000 goldfish of about 40 species.
This facility not only attracts goldfish, but the entire room is an artwork based on the concept of goldfish. Using a variety of materials such as projection mapping, flowers, terrariums, and mirror balls, goldfish of Yamato Koriyama, from familiar varieties to rare species, gracefully swim among the works of art created by various artists.
There are many photo-friendly spots where visitors can enjoy taking pictures with their cameras.
Unlike other goldfish exhibits, this exhibit will provide both "newcomers" and "fish lovers" with an emotional experience that will stimulate all five senses. It also features “Trick Art” where you can “ride” on a goldfish or enter a goldfish bowl. You can take fun pictures using optical illusions.
“Trick Art”
My child absolutely enjoyed all the pretty colors. I highly recommend this place.
Things to note:
• This place is inside a shopping building center

name: Heisei Haibara Children's Forest Park 平成榛原子供のもり公園 in Uda City
description:
Family friendly park to camp and barbecue
Here’s a park full of greenery where you can enjoy camping, barbecues, and all kinds of fun athletic activities.
This park skillfully utilizes the slopes of the mountain in Uda City, Nara Prefecture. The spacious park surrounded by greenery is fully equipped with sports facilities such as a campsite, a baseball field, and a soccer field. At the top of a small hill is Dinosaur Country, which is equipped with a corridor-shaped athletic playground equipment with a total length of 400m, echoing the sounds of happy children playing. You can enjoy a barbecue along the banks of the Udagawa River.
Things to note:
• There is no where to buy food so bring your own food
• There is a dedicated area specifically for ball play (catch, badminton, frisbee)
• There is an open space lawn which may be ideal for picnics. Cheap picnic mats and pop-up tents are available.
• You can play on the lawn slide, so it is recommended to bring something that you can spread out and slide on
• In the summer, you can play in the water, so
bring a towel

name: Kashihara Children's Museum of Science in 橿原市立こども科学館 Kashihara city
description:
Another great place for rainy days. Children can use their five senses here to explore this museum geared towards them. ￼
In addition to various science-related exhibits focusing on the sciences such as astronomy, electricity, magnets, sound, light, and force, there is also a "Becoming an Astronaut" exhibit where you can wear a space suit, experiment with a different theme each month, mini crafts, and much more. There are many zones where you can learn science while having fun. Here’s a list of a few:
○ Force and Gravity Zone / Chikara no hataraki zōn / 力のはたらきゾーン
Where children can learn how force applied to tools and objects works.
○ Electricity and Magnetism Zone / Denki to jishaku no hataraki zōn / 電気と磁石のはたらきゾーン
Where children can learn, in a fun way, the principles of electricity and magnets, which work in various ways in our everyday lives.
○ Properties of Light and Sound Zone / Hikari to oto no seishitsu zōn / 光と音の性質ゾーン
We all know what light and sound are, but they are actually difficult scientific concepts to grasp. Here, through play, children can begin to understand the nature of light and sound.
○ Spaceship Simulator
Piloting an airship that takes off from a base on a planet, visitors aim for the earth while completing various missions.
The number of participants is 1 captain (pilot) and 4 crew members.
○ Air Rocket
Participants experience launching a rocket made of plastic bottles and learn the basic principles of rockets.
○ Foucault's pendulum
Watch the orbit of the pendulum
○ Experimental Workshop
There is a teacher here who explains various scientific phenomenas in an easy-to-understand way and conducts mini experiments for you to watch. There is also a Mini Craft Workshop where you can create simple crafts.
In addition to all of this, there are limited-time events held seasonally:
During Golden Week in May is the "Children's Day Event" (kodomo no hi event)
During Summer Vacation in August there’s the “Summer Vacation Event” (Natsu Yasumi event)
In November, there’s the “Kansai Culture Day Event"
There’s the “Science Festival" in March, etc.
So there are all kinds of events to look forward to throughout the year.
